theses.alab:
ALAB — Astera Labs
Book: AI Trade · Opening weight 5.0% · Horizon 12 months
SOURCED BY THE EMERGING-THEME RADAR (IPS 3b), first run, 2026-08-14.

WHY WE OWN IT
Astera sells the connectivity silicon — signal conditioning and AI fabric — that
holds large GPU clusters together. As clusters scale, the number of these parts
per GPU rises. It is a volume-times-attach-rate business layered on top of the
same buildout the rest of the book owns, but with a different failure mode than
the compute names.

VALUATION — the richest absolute multiple on the desk
  Price $321.61 · Market cap $55.79B
  Trailing P/E 158.42 · Forward P/E 57.31   ← forward BELOW trailing
  Revenue +98.5% y/y · EPS $2.03 (+240.2%)
  Consensus target $391.77 = +21.8% upside, 26 analysts
  Growth-adjusted 0.58 — among the best on the desk
  52-week range $97.89–$499.48 — currently 36% BELOW the high

This is the clearest illustration of why the gate uses a growth-adjusted
multiple rather than a raw one. 57x forward earnings looks indefensible until
you divide by 98.5% revenue growth and get 0.58, better than almost anything
else owned. Both facts are true at once.

CLAIMS AND VERIFICATION
  CLAIM  Record quarterly revenue of $392.4M, +27% sequentially and +104% y/y.
  VERIFIED  Company reporting via stockanalysis.com, 14 Aug 2026.

  CLAIM  Q3 guidance of $540–560M.
  VERIFIED  Same source. That implies roughly +38% sequential growth, which is
  the single most impressive forward number I have found on this desk.

WHY IT IS ONLY 5%
A 57x forward multiple prices in flawless execution. One guidance miss and the
multiple compresses violently — the 36% drawdown from its high already shows
how that behaves. High conviction in the business, deliberately small position,
because the price allows no room for error.

WHAT WOULD MAKE ME WRONG
  · Any sequential guidance miss
  · Hyperscalers in-sourcing connectivity silicon
  · Growth decelerating below ~50% while the multiple stays above 50x
theses.amd:
AMD — Advanced Micro Devices
Book: AI Trade · Opening weight 11.0% · Horizon 12+ months

WHY WE OWN IT
The AI trade is rotating from training to inference, and inference is a
memory-bound problem rather than a raw-FLOPS problem. That shift is the single
most important structural change in this sector right now, and AMD is better
positioned in inference than it ever was in training. This is the highest-
conviction name in the book and it gets the largest weight.

CLAIMS AND VERIFICATION

  CLAIM  Q2 2026 revenue was $11.5B, up 50% year over year.
  VERIFIED  AMD investor relations, Q2 2026 results release (primary source).
  Prior-year comparison $7.685B. Confirms.

  CLAIM  Data center revenue grew 107% y/y to $6.718B, now 58% of the company.
  VERIFIED  Same primary source. This is the number that matters: the data
  center segment has crossed from a side business into the majority of AMD.

  CLAIM  Margins are expanding, not being bought with price cuts.
  VERIFIED  Non-GAAP gross margin 56% vs 43% a year ago. GAAP EPS $1.38,
  +156% y/y. Growth is falling through to profit.

  CLAIM  Q3 2026 guidance is ~$13B, +41% y/y.
  VERIFIED  Company guidance in the same release, with a stated +/- $300M band.

  CLAIM  AMD holds large-scale inference agreements with OpenAI, Meta,
  Microsoft and Anthropic.
  PARTIALLY CONFIRMED  Widely reported and consistent with company statements
  at Advancing AI 2026, but I did not locate signed-contract terms in a filing.
  Treated as supporting color, NOT as the load-bearing reason to own this.

  CLAIM  Inference TAM reaches $1.3T by 2032 (32% CAGR), about 2x training.
  UNVERIFIED  Sourced to Bloomberg Intelligence via secondary reporting. A
  forecast, not a fact. Directionally useful, not relied upon.

WHAT WOULD MAKE ME WRONG
  · Data center growth decelerating below ~40% y/y for two straight quarters
  · Gross margin rolling back under 50%
  · A named hyperscaler publicly standardizing away from AMD for inference
  · Total AI capex guidance across hyperscalers being cut

EXIT CONDITIONS
Thesis-driven, plus the book's hard -20% stop from cost.

theses.cbrs:
CBRS — Cerebras Systems
Book: Moonshot · Opening weight 8.0% · Horizon 12 months

WHY WE OWN IT
This is the one name that currently fits the mandate you described: enormous
sentiment, credible high price targets, a story running well ahead of profits,
and a business early enough that the outcome is genuinely undecided. Wafer-scale
chips with embedded SRAM are architecturally well-suited to exactly the
inference workloads the market is rotating toward.

CLAIMS AND VERIFICATION  (all figures from Cerebras investor relations, Q1 2026
release — primary source)

  CLAIM  Q1 2026 revenue of $193.4M, up 94% year over year.
  VERIFIED  Confirms. Core revenue $191.3M, +92%.

  CLAIM  Cloud and services revenue up 178% y/y to $82.8M.
  VERIFIED  Confirms. The mix shift toward recurring cloud revenue is the most
  encouraging line in the release and is the actual reason I am buying.

  CLAIM  FY2026 core revenue guidance of $855-865M, ~+69% y/y at midpoint.
  VERIFIED  Company guidance. Confirms.

  CLAIM  A $20B+ multi-year OpenAI agreement covering 750MW of capacity.
  VERIFIED  Disclosed by the company.

  CLAIM  It is roughly break-even, not deeply lossmaking.
  VERIFIED  GAAP net loss $(14.0)M, core net loss $(2.5)M on $193M revenue.
  Unusual for a company at this growth rate and it materially de-risks the story.

THE RISKS, STATED PLAINLY  — I am not burying these

  1. CUSTOMER CONCENTRATION. The company itself discloses dependence on "a
     limited number of significant customers, including OpenAI, Group 42
     Holding Ltd, Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence, and
     AWS." If OpenAI reworks its commitment, the thesis breaks in one press
     release. This is the single largest risk and it is disclosed by them, not
     discovered by me.

  2. IPO'd 14 May 2026 — about three months of public history. There are no
     four public quarters to check management's guidance credibility against.
     I cannot yet grade whether they do what they say.

  3. GROSS MARGIN GUIDANCE OF 38-41% for FY26, DOWN from 47% core in Q1. The
     company is guiding its own margins lower. That is either scale-up cost or
     pricing pressure, and I do not yet know which.

  4. Priced for a great outcome after the largest IPO of 2026.

WHY IT IS 8% AND NOT MORE
Four disclosed risks, three months of public history, and margin guidance
moving the wrong way. Conviction in the thesis does not entitle it to size.

EXIT CONDITIONS
  · Any material change to the OpenAI relationship
  · FY26 core revenue guidance cut below $855M
  · Gross margin guided below 35%
  · The book's hard -25% stop from cost
theses.ceg:
CEG — Constellation Energy
Book: AI Trade · Opening weight 7.5% · Horizon 12+ months

WHY WE OWN IT
The binding constraint on AI is shifting from chips to electricity. Data
centers need power that is carbon-free, always-on, and available at scale, and
in the United States that describes the existing nuclear fleet almost uniquely.
Constellation owns the largest one. This is the book's answer to the question
"what breaks first," and it is not correlated with the semiconductor names.

CLAIMS AND VERIFICATION

  CLAIM  AI data center demand is driving an electricity supercycle, with power
  a genuine constraint on the buildout.
  VERIFIED  GE Vernova Q2 2026 reported $2.7B of data center orders in
  Electrification alone, first-half data center orders above $5B (more than
  double all of 2025), and gas power "mostly sold out through 2030." Independent
  confirmation that power, not compute, is the scarce input.

  CLAIM  Constellation specifically has contracted nuclear capacity to
  hyperscaler data centers.
  UNVERIFIED  I did not confirm current contract terms in a primary filing this
  session. This is the weakest-verified position in the book and is sized
  accordingly at 7.5%. It is on the list for primary-source verification at the
  first monthly cycle, and I will cut it if the specifics do not hold up.

WHAT WOULD MAKE ME WRONG
  · Power turning out not to be a binding constraint (watch GEV order growth)
  · Adverse regulatory treatment of behind-the-meter data center deals
theses.cohr:
COHR — Coherent Corp
Book: AI Trade · Opening weight 6.5% · Horizon 12+ months
SOURCED BY THE EMERGING-THEME RADAR (IPS 3b), first run, 2026-08-14.

WHY WE OWN IT
The AI bottleneck is migrating from the chip to the link between chips. At
cluster scale, copper runs out of headroom on power and latency before it runs
out of bandwidth, which forces optics into the package. Broadcom's own framing
is the tell: "our switches and XPUs are going to be lower power with optics than
with copper." Optics justify themselves on efficiency, not just speed — which
means adoption is driven by the electricity bill, the hardest constraint there is.

Coherent makes the optoelectronic components and engineered materials this
transition runs on.

VALUATION
  Price $325.83 · Market cap $63.75B
  Trailing P/E 79.09 · Forward P/E 35.20   ← forward BELOW trailing
  Revenue +22.5% y/y · Net income +1,530.7% y/y
  Consensus target $410.76 = +26.1% upside, 22 analysts
  Growth-adjusted 1.56 vs the 2.0 limit
  52-week range $84.35–$440.00 — currently 26% BELOW the high

That last line matters as much as the multiple. The optics complex has rallied
hard, and buying a theme after it runs is how you lose money being right. This
one has already given back a quarter of its move.

CLAIMS AND VERIFICATION
  CLAIM  The Open Compute Interconnect standard was founded by AMD, Broadcom,
  NVIDIA, Meta, Microsoft and OpenAI.
  VERIFIED  OFC 2026 conference coverage. When six competitors agree a standard,
  the direction is settled and only the timing is in question.

  CLAIM  Volume production for CPO/silicon photonics integration targets 2028,
  with full GPU-HBM package integration around 2029.
  PARTIALLY CONFIRMED  Conference reporting, not company guidance. An industry
  roadmap, and roadmaps slip.

  CLAIM  NVIDIA invested $2B in Lumentum as part of a ~$4B optical strategy.
  PARTIALLY CONFIRMED  Secondary reporting. Used as evidence the theme is real,
  NOT as a reason to own this specific name.

WHAT WOULD MAKE ME WRONG
  · CPO timelines slipping past 2028 — the whole thesis is timing
  · Hyperscalers standardizing on pluggable optics for longer than expected
  · 35x forward compressing toward the components-sector average

theses.mu:
MU — Micron Technology
Book: AI Trade · Opening weight 10.0% · Horizon 12+ months
NEW POSITION — the memory leg this book was missing.

WHY WE OWN IT
Inference is a memory-bound problem, not a FLOPS-bound one. Every argument in
this book about the rotation from training to inference implies memory demand,
and until now the book had no memory exposure at all. That was a hole.

Micron is also, by a wide margin, the cheapest thing on this desk.

VALUATION  (the reason this is a large position)
  Price $971.66 · Market cap $1.10T
  Trailing P/E 21.43 · FORWARD P/E 6.61
  Revenue +167% y/y · EPS +705.7% y/y
  Consensus target $1,501.98 = +54.6% upside, 46 analysts, Strong Buy
  Growth-adjusted multiple 0.04 vs the 2.0 limit

A 6.61x forward multiple on a company growing revenue 167% is not a rounding
error, it is a statement. The market is saying: these are peak-cycle earnings
and they will collapse, so we refuse to capitalize them. That is the memory
discount, and historically the market has often been right to apply it.

THE ACTUAL BET, STATED HONESTLY
I am betting this cycle is structurally different, for one specific reason:
HBM for AI accelerators is contracted years forward, not sold spot like
commodity DRAM. Contracted capacity does not behave like a commodity glut.

  CLAIM  The memory shortage may persist past 2030.
  PARTIALLY CONFIRMED  Attributed to SK Hynix via secondary reporting. It is a
  competitor's forecast, not a fact, and forecasts from people who benefit from
  scarcity deserve discounting. Directional support only.

  CLAIM  Revenue +167% y/y, forward P/E 6.61, target $1,501.98.
  VERIFIED  stockanalysis.com, 14 Aug 2026.

WHAT WOULD MAKE ME WRONG — and this is a real risk, not a formality
  · The market is simply right: HBM capacity floods in, pricing breaks, and the
    6.61x forward multiple turns out to be 6.61x on earnings that halve
  · DRAM contract pricing rolling over
  · Any hyperscaler cutting memory procurement guidance

If the multiple is a trap, it is a trap I walked into knowingly. A cheap
cyclical at the top of its cycle is the oldest mistake in equities. I am sizing
this at 10% rather than the 12% cap for exactly that reason.

that is mostly Nvidia is really just a single-stock bet wearing a costume.

  CLAIM  Nvidia is extending from training into inference silicon, including
  Groq-derived LPU technology with embedded SRAM for the decode phase.
  PARTIALLY CONFIRMED  Reported by Motley Fool (Aug 2026) and consistent with
  the broader inference narrative. I did NOT verify the acquisition terms in a
  filing. Supporting color only.

  CLAIM  Hyperscaler 2026 capex expectations run near $840B, up from $487B in
  early February 2026.
  VERIFIED  Axios, 5 Aug 2026, citing tracked hyperscaler guidance. This is the
  demand curve underneath the whole book, and it is still revising upward.

WHAT WOULD MAKE ME WRONG
  · Hyperscaler capex guidance revised DOWN — the cleanest single tell
  · Custom ASICs (Broadcom/Google TPU) taking visible inference share
  · Gross margin compression signaling lost pricing power

RISK I AM ACCEPTING KNOWINGLY
This is a consensus long at a record-high market. I am not being paid for
originality here; I am being paid not to be cute about the largest and most
obvious beneficiary of the largest capex cycle in the sector's history.

theses.unh:
UNH — UnitedHealth Group
Book: Core · Opening weight 6.5% · Horizon multi-year
NEW POSITION — the non-technology ballast.

WHY WE OWN IT
After the valuation gate finished, the Core book was four mega-cap technology
names and a healthcare ETF. That is not a diversified portfolio, it is an AI bet
with extra steps — and it would have been highly correlated with the AI book.
UNH is the deliberate correction.

VALUATION — a documented edge case
  Price $401.73 · Market cap $360.59B
  Trailing P/E 25.86 · Forward P/E 18.88  ← forward BELOW trailing
  Trailing EPS $15.53, DOWN 32.8% y/y
  Consensus target $475.23 = +18.3% upside, 27 analysts, Buy

A naive growth-adjusted test would fail this: you cannot divide a multiple by
negative growth. But the trailing decline IS the opportunity — the multiple has
already de-rated for it. Forward P/E of 18.88 against trailing 25.86 implies
roughly 37% forward earnings recovery, giving a growth-adjusted figure of 0.51.

That method is now written into IPS 3a and research/valuation.json, before the
fact, precisely so it cannot be applied selectively to rescue names I like.

  CLAIM  "UnitedHealth blows past estimates, hikes earnings outlook as it reins
  in costs."
  PARTIALLY CONFIRMED  Reported via stockanalysis.com's news summary. The beat
  and raise is consistent with forward P/E sitting below trailing. I did NOT
  read the primary release this session. Flagged for verification.

WHAT WOULD MAKE ME WRONG
  · Medical loss ratio deteriorating again
  · Medicare Advantage rate or regulatory pressure
  · The recovery in forward estimates not materializing in the next two prints
theses.vrt:
VRT — Vertiv Holdings
Book: AI Trade · Opening weight 5.5% · Horizon 12 months
NEW POSITION — thermal and power distribution inside the rack.

WHY WE OWN IT
Rack densities are rising faster than air cooling can handle, which forces
liquid cooling. Vertiv sells the thermal management and power distribution that
sits between the utility feed and the GPU. It is the least glamorous link in the
chain and one of the hardest to design around.

VALUATION — the weakest pass in the book
  Price $293.84 · Market cap $113.12B
  Trailing P/E 66.50 · Forward P/E 37.69
  Revenue +26.2% y/y · EPS +168.8% (2025)
  Consensus target $338.15 = +15.08% upside, 28 analysts, Strong Buy
  Growth-adjusted multiple 1.44 vs the 2.0 limit

It clears the 15% upside floor by 0.08 percentage points. That is a pass, and
it is a pass I am not proud of. Hence the smallest position in the book.

  CLAIM  Recent results were mixed; management called the issues "a temporary
  issue" relating to project timing and supply chain.
  VERIFIED as a quote. Treated with the skepticism that phrase deserves — it is

WHAT WOULD MAKE ME WRONG

Two reasons, and I want to be straight about the second one.

watchlist._purpose: Emerging theme radar. The client's instruction: space data centers was an EXAMPLE of a class - themes with low absolute chatter and rising interest, where the upside is caught early. This file tracks those themes between cycles, so the hunt is systematic rather than whatever I happened to think of that week. Reviewed every two weeks. IPS 3b.

_scoring.chatter: LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH - absolute mainstream coverage. LOW is what we want.
_scoring.trajectory: RISING / FLAT / FALLING - direction of interest. RISING + LOW is the target quadrant.
_scoring.capital_committed: Has real money moved? Funding rounds, capex line items, regulatory filings. Money moves before articles do.
_scoring.vehicle_quality: GOOD / DILUTED / NONE - is there a public company whose economics actually concentrate the theme? This is the test most themes fail.
_scoring.time_to_pnl: When does this hit an income statement?

themes.name: Co-packaged optics / silicon photonics
themes.thesis: The AI bottleneck is moving from the chip to the interconnect between chips. Copper is running out of headroom on power and latency at cluster scale, forcing optics directly into the package. Broadcom's framing is the tell: 'our switches and XPUs are going to be lower power with optics than with copper' - optics justify themselves on efficiency, not just bandwidth.
themes.capital_committed: NVIDIA invested $2B in Lumentum as part of a reported $4B optical strategy. The Open Compute Interconnect standard was founded by AMD, Broadcom, NVIDIA, Meta, Microsoft and OpenAI together. Samsung and ST are bringing silicon photonics to 300mm wafer platforms.
themes.time_to_pnl: Revenue now, inflection at 2028 volume production for CPO integration; 2029 for full GPU-HBM package integration.

vehicles.COHR: BOUGHT. Passes the gate: 35.20x fwd, +26.1% upside, forward BELOW trailing. Trades 26% below its 52-week high, so not chasing a top.
vehicles.ALAB: BOUGHT. Passes: 57.31x fwd but revenue +98.5% gives 0.58 growth-adjusted. Q3 guided $540-560M vs $392.4M actual.
vehicles.LITE: REJECTED - already ran. $111.20 to $926.14 across the 52-week range, market cap +888% y/y. Negative trailing earnings. The theme is real; this vehicle is late. Being right about a theme and buying it at 8x is still losing.
vehicles.MRVL/AVGO/NVDA: Already held or adjacent exposure via AVGO and NVDA.

themes.name: Power transformers and grain-oriented electrical steel
themes.thesis: A real, well-documented hard constraint on the AI buildout: power transformer lead times went from ~50 weeks in 2021 to ~120 weeks by 2024 (Wood Mackenzie), large units run 80-210 weeks, prices are up 60-80% since Jan 2020, and only ~20% of US demand can be met domestically. It slows the PACE of the buildout and favours the supply-constrained names. CORRECTION 2026-08-14: I originally carried a '30-50% of 2026 capacity cancelled' bear claim here as a risk to this desk's own AI book. On verification that framing is substantially overstated — SemiAnalysis showed the underlying denominator is off by multiples, the shortfall sits in speculative announcements that were never real 2026 projects, and their own forecast moved ~1% in six months. Meanwhile hyperscaler capex was RAISED to $725B (+77% y/y). Constraint: real. Demand threat: not supported. See the full note below.
themes.capital_committed: Cleveland-Cliffs' Butler Works is the only domestic producer of grain-oriented electrical steel and the only domestic source of the high-permeability grade used in power transformers. Its $170M expansion does not arrive until 2028.
themes.time_to_pnl: Now, but buried inside larger businesses.

vehicles.CLF: REJECTED. The perfect narrative and the wrong vehicle. Consensus target $11.80 against an $11.90 price = -0.8% DOWNSIDE, Hold rating from 13 analysts, and the company is lossmaking (-$876M net income, EPS -$1.60). The GOES monopoly is a rounding error inside $19.2B of commodity steel revenue that mostly serves autos. An under-covered theme is only investable if some vehicle's economics actually concentrate it.
vehicles._todo: Still the highest-priority open item: find a liquid US-listed pure-play transformer or grid-equipment vehicle. Screen Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy, Prolec, Hammond Power for a US listing or ADR clearing IPS 8 liquidity.

themes.note:
VERIFIED AND REVISED 2026-08-14. I initially flagged '30-50% of announced data center capacity may slip' as a risk to this desk's AI book, on the strength of one Medium post and a Forbes piece. That was below the evidence standard I apply to buying a stock, so it should not have been enough to argue against one. On checking:

SOURCE OF THE CLAIM: Currence, an energy intelligence firm, tracking 777 announced AI factories >50MW. ~190GW announced since 2024; 16GW scheduled for 2026 operation; ~5GW under construction.

THE REBUTTAL (SemiAnalysis, the most credible source in this niche, published specifically to correct this): (1) the 5GW denominator is 'off by multiples' — their satellite imagery shows the top TWO hyperscalers alone exceed 5GW under construction; (2) the cancellations cluster in early-stage speculative announcements lacking site control, financing or interconnection — projects never realistic for 2026 anyway; (3) SemiAnalysis's own year-end 2026 North America hyperscaler self-build forecast moved only ~1% over six months, colocation under 5% — the people modeling this most carefully barely changed their numbers; (4) the meme traces to an April 2026 Bloomberg piece about Chinese electrical parts, sharpened into clickbait downstream.

ALSO: 'delayed' is not 'cancelled'. Currence itself measures timeline slippage, not abandonment. Delays push revenue right; they do not destroy it.

MEANWHILE THE DEMAND SIDE ACCELERATED: 2026 hyperscaler capex $725B, up 77% from $410B in 2025 — MSFT $190B, Alphabet up to $190B (+$5B), Meta $145B+ (+$10B). Guidance RAISED, not cut. And the revenue is showing up: Google Cloud +63% y/y to $20B/quarter, Meta +33% to $56.3B, Alphabet net income +81% to $62.6B. GE Vernova's Q2 call disclosed Gas Power capacity rising to 30GW by 2030, near-full utilization of 2030 slots, and >50% of 2031 capacity contracted by year-end 2026 — contracted, prepaid, multi-year commitments are the opposite of a demand air pocket.

CONCLUSION: the transformer constraint is real and well documented (Wood Mackenzie: lead times 50wk in 2021 to 120wk by 2024, large units 80-210wk, prices +60-80% since Jan 2020, only ~20% of US demand met domestically). It slows the PACE of buildout. It does not undermine the demand thesis, and the '30-50% cancelled' framing is substantially overstated. I am REMOVING this as a bear case against the AI book and keeping it as a TIMING consideration that favours the supply-constrained names over those needing new capacity online fast.

WHAT I GOT WRONG: I amplified a thinly-sourced bear claim without checking it, in the same session I wrote a rule requiring primary-source verification. The client asked me to explain it, which is what surfaced the error.
sources: The Geopolitical Economist on the transformer shortage
tripwires: GE Vernova order growth decelerating (quarterly, public)
Any hyperscaler CUTTING capex guidance — none have; all raised
Transformer lead times extending materially beyond ~120-128 weeks
SemiAnalysis revising its self-build forecast down by more than 5%

themes.name: Space / orbital data centers
themes.thesis: Terrestrial data centers are constrained by land, power and water. Orbital compute is constrained by launch cost, which falls on a technology curve rather than a resource curve.
themes.capital_committed: Blue Origin filed for 51,600 data center satellites. Starcloud reached a $1.1B valuation. Meta signed a space-based power agreement with Overview Energy. Google's Project Suncatcher completed radiation testing with two prototypes planned for early 2027. SpaceX targets Starmind AI1 as early as 2027 using NVIDIA Vera CPUs and Rubin GPUs.

vehicles.NVDA: HELD. Disclosed $21B stake in SpaceX plus the Starmind AI1 compute partnership. The cleanest exposure, and free inside a position owned for other reasons.
vehicles.RKLB: MOONSHOT-PENDING. 2 of 4 Moonshot criteria verified. Trades 47% below its 52-week high, so not disqualified for having run.
vehicles._todo: CLIENT DIRECTION 2026-08-14, priority order. PRIMARY: public companies holding disclosed stakes in private space/AI-infrastructure leaders. NVDA's $21B in SpaceX is the model and is already owned free inside a position held for other reasons — screen for others of that shape, since it converts private-market exposure into something liquid and gate-checkable. SECONDARY, pursue if research supports it: (a) radiation-hardened semiconductors — the highest-quality bottleneck in the chain, few qualified suppliers, Intel Starfire and Microchip as starting points; (b) launch capacity — Blue Origin's 51,600-satellite filing and Starcloud need lift, RKLB the main listed pure-play, and the open question is whether launch is a constraint or a commodity; (c) thermal/power/structures — cooling in vacuum is an unsolved engineering problem, Redwire and satellite component makers. The client noted these are unfamiliar to them, so any position here needs the thesis written for someone starting from zero, not for someone who already follows the sector.

themes.note: Honest economics: orbital compute currently costs ~4x terrestrial ($8.64 vs $2.37 per GPU-hour). This is 2027+ optionality, not a 2026 revenue story. Do not let a good narrative become a valuation argument.
sources: Fierce Network on space data centers

themes.thesis: Inference moving off the data center and into machines that act on the world. Distinct from the buildout trade because the economics are unit-volume driven rather than capex driven.
themes.capital_committed: Being named as a distinct investment theme in Asian markets; hardware startup funding concentrating on edge compute and robotics infrastructure.

themes.name: How the AI buildout is actually being financed
themes.thesis: Hyperscaler 2026 capex expectations ran to roughly $840B, up from $487B in early February. Capex is now growing faster than the revenue it supports. That gap has to be financed somewhere - vendor financing, private credit, SPVs, debt. Follow the money and you find both a risk indicator for the whole desk and possibly a beneficiary.
themes.capital_committed: NVIDIA advancing a reported $500B AI infrastructure financing initiative with financial partners. AMD completed a record $5B bond sale.
themes.note: This is the theme most likely to matter to the desk as a WARNING rather than an opportunity. If AI capex is increasingly debt-financed, the buildout becomes rate-sensitive and the whole AI book inherits that sensitivity. Highest-priority monitoring item.

_open_questions: PRIMARY for 2026-08-28: which public companies hold disclosed stakes in private space / AI-infra leaders? NVDA/SpaceX is the template. This converts private exposure into a liquid, gate-checkable position.
Listed SUPPLIERS to private space-compute leaders — client-directed priority for the 2026-08-28 cycle.
Is there a liquid US-listed pure-play on power transformers? Highest-value unanswered question on this list.
What is the actual debt share of 2026 hyperscaler capex? Determines how rate-sensitive the AI book really is.

Does anything in physical AI clear IPS 8 on liquidity and venue?

_lesson_log.lesson: Applied the verification standard asymmetrically: demanded primary sources before BUYING, accepted a Medium post before flagging a RISK. Bear claims need the same evidence bar as bull claims. A comfortable-sounding caution is still a claim.
_lesson_log.cost: None — caught before it changed any position.
_lesson_log.fix: IPS 4 now applies explicitly to risk claims as well as thesis claims.
